attempts.input: Two tabs (A, B) on the same project 'Base'. Both tabs type a new project name in the same instant (Promise.all fill 'A-edit'/'B-edit'), so their 300 ms save timers fire within milliseconds. Goal: reach the 'conflict' path (keepThisTab(false)), then Undo back to the last saved state and press 'Keep this tab's copy', expecting 'Saved' with nothing written (saveNow skips the write when text === lastSavedText).
attempts.observed: 8 trials. The conflict path was never reached: every time the other tab's storage event arrived first and the tab stopped saving with the 'This project was just changed in another tab or window' notice (event path, which resets lastSavedText). Trial 7: BOTH tabs stopped saving and stored = 'B-edit', i.e. B's write replaced A's already-saved write without B detecting a conflict (A still had its work on screen). The undo-then-keep follow-up could not be run.

attempts.input: (a) Tab A stops saving because tab B renamed the project to 'B-edit'; A then types 'A-typed-while-held' and presses F5. (b) Same, but A is closed (runBeforeUnload) the instant after typing. (c) Ordinary (saving) tab A types and is closed within the 300 ms save delay.
attempts.observed: (a) After F5, A shows 'B-edit', status 'Saved in this browser, on this computer', and NO notice at all; A's typed work exists only as a kept copy ('The work in the project “A-typed-while-held” that was not yet saved when you left or reloaded the page.'), listed on the Summary under 'Copies the Studio kept for you' with a download button. Work kept, but the reload says nothing about it: the owner sees the other tab's project with no hint that their own typing went to the Summary. (b) Kept copy present, complete. (c) Stored = 'A-closed-within-300ms' (written on leaving); B stopped saving correctly.

attempts.input: Two tabs type in the same instant; tab A is closed the moment its status line reads 'Saved…' (polling every 5 ms). 12 trials. Check that A's work is still saved or kept.
attempts.observed: 0 of 12 trials lost A's work. 10 trials: A said 'Saved in this browser, on this computer', stored = A's name, B stopped saving. 2 trials: A had already stopped saving; its work was kept as a copy on close.

attempts.input: Browser Back button: tab A navigates away to another page, tab B renames the project to 'B-edit', tab A presses Back; then A types and (if stopped) Undo + 'Keep this tab's copy'.
attempts.observed: Chromium did not restore A from the back-forward cache (page reloaded fresh; pageshow persisted = null). A showed 'B-edit' and 'Saved…', which was true. A's next edit saved normally. No stale page, no win.

attempts.input: Three tabs. A renames to 'A-edit-n' and saves; B and C stop saving and each types new work ('B-more-n', 'C-more-n'). Then, in the same instant in B and C: mode reload = press 'Reload to see the other copy'; mode close = close both tabs (runBeforeUnload); mode keep = press 'Keep this tab's copy'. 4 trials per mode. Look for each piece of work in the stored project, the kept copies, or the tab's screen.
attempts.observed: reload mode: 4/4 complete (both kept copies present). close mode: trial 2 lost 'C-more-2' entirely: kept = ['B-more-2'] only, stored = 'A-edit-2', and no leave-page question appeared (the second tab's kept copy was overwritten by the first tab's write to the shared kept-copies list). keep mode: no piece missing while tabs were open, but stored and kept disagreed with what the screens showed (followed up in attempts 6 and 7).

attempts.input: Part 1 (6 trials): same three-tab setup; press 'Keep this tab's copy' in B and C in the same instant, read both status lines, then close B and C at once. Part 2 (10 trials): close two stopped tabs B and C at once (the owner closes the browser window), without pressing anything.
attempts.observed: Part 1: work lost silently in 5 of 6 trials. Trials 2 and 4: BOTH B and C said 'Saved in this browser, on this computer' with no notice, yet the store held only one of them (trial 2: stored = 'B-more-2'; C's screen showed 'C-more-2' and said Saved). After both tabs were closed, 'C-more-2' (trial 4: 'B-more-4') was nowhere: not stored, not in the kept copies, and no leave-page question was asked. Trials 1, 5, 6: both tabs said 'Not saving: see the notice at the top of the page'; after closing, one tab's work (e.g. 'B-more-1') was nowhere and no question was asked. Source reading: leaveSafely() returns 'safe' when the text equals lastSavedText even in a stopped tab, and that text had been overwritten by the other tab's write. Cause: the other tab's 'keep the other copy' step and the saveBrowserNow conflict check read a stale localStorage value (each tab process has its own cache), so neither noticed. Part 2: 1 of 10 trials lost a tab's work ('C-more-2'): the kept-copies list is read-modify-written by both closing tabs, so one kept copy replaced the other. No notice anywhere.

attempts.input: Attack 6 part 1 with a human-sized pause between the two presses of 'Keep this tab's copy' (B first, then C after 0, 50, 150, 400, 1000 ms). 3 trials per gap. Then close both tabs at once and accept any leave-page question.
attempts.observed: Gap 0 ms: 3/3 trials lost B's work silently ('B-more-n' not stored, not kept; zero leave-page questions), with both tabs showing 'Not saving…' before closing. Gaps 50, 150, 400, 1000 ms: 0 losses; B was correctly stopped, and on closing its work was kept; C said 'Saved…' truthfully. Conclusion: the 'Keep this tab's copy' double-press loss needs two presses within a few milliseconds, which one person with one mouse cannot do. Closing several stopped tabs at once (closing the window, attempt 6 part 2) is the realistic trigger, and there the loss is rare (about 1 in 10 to 1 in 4).
